<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 650 550" width="650" height="550">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="white" />

  <defs>
    <!-- Arrowhead for North arrow -->
    <marker id="arrow" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="10" refX="5" refY="5" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M 0 10 L 5 0 L 10 10 z" fill="black" />
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <g font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" fill="black">
    <!-- Points coordinates based on calculations:
         Let B = (180, 420)
         D is due North of B, so D = (180, 200) -> distance BD = 220 px (represents some scale)
         Let's set precise coordinates to fit the geometry:
         B = (200, 430)
         D = (200, 210)  [vector BD goes straight up]
         C: CD = 9m, angle BCD = 85, angle DBC = 30 at B? Wait, B is at bottom, D is North, C is right.
         Let's position B, C, D to roughly match the triangle BCD with CD=9, BD=x, BC=y, ∠DBC=30°, ∠DCB=85°.
         Let's place B at (220, 420)
         D at (220, 220) [North of B]
         North arrow goes from D upwards to (220, 140), with "N" at top.
         For triangle BCD:
         B = (220, 420), D = (220, 220). BD = 200 units.
         ∠DBC = 30° at B. Ray BC goes down-right from B at angle 30° to BD?
         Wait, D is North of B. If ∠DBC = 30°, C is to the east of the line BD.
         Let's check angle DBC = 30°. Vector BD is (0, -1). 30° east of North is direction (sin 30°, -cos 30°) = (0.5, -0.866).
         Let's use exact coordinates for points to make a clean diagram:
         B = (220, 420)
         D = (220, 230)  (Vertical line up to North)
         Actually let's scale:
         B = (200, 440)
         D = (200, 230)
         North arrow: line from (200, 230) to (200, 140) with label N at (200, 130).
         ∠DBC = 30°: Line BC goes from B at 30° to BD. Since BD is vertical upwards, 30° clockwise from North is angle 60° above horizontal, or vector (sin 30°, -cos 30°).
         Let C be at some distance from B. Using sine rule on BCD:
         CD/sin(30) = BC/sin(BDC) = BD/sin(85)
         Here CD = 9, ∠DCB = 85°, ∠DBC = 30° => ∠BDC = 180 - 85 - 30 = 65°
         BD = 9 * sin(85°) / sin(65°) ≈ 9 * 0.9962 / 0.9063 ≈ 9.89 m
         BC = 9 * sin(65°) / sin(85°) ? No, BC / sin(65°) = 9 / sin(30°) => BC = 9 * sin(65°) / 0.5 ≈ 16.3 m.
         Let's place C relative to B: distance BC = 163 px at angle 30° east of North.
         B = (200, 450)
         C = (200 + 163*sin(30°), 450 - 163*cos(30°)) = (200 + 81.5, 450 - 141.1) = (281.5, 308.9) -> let's round: C = (282, 309).
         Check D: D is North of B, so D = (200, 450 - BD_scaled).
         If BD = 9.89 m (scale 10 px per metre approx -> 99 px):
         D = (200, 450 - 99) = (200, 351).
         Wait, earlier D was (200, 230). Let's use scale 15 px / m:
         CD = 9m -> 135 px
         BD = 9.89m -> 148 px
         AB = 14.5m -> 217 px
         AD = 6m -> 90 px
         Let's set:
         B = (220, 450)
         D = (220, 450 - 148) = (220, 302)
         C: angle DBC = 30° east of North.
         C_x = 220 + 135 * ... wait, BC = 16.3m -> 244 px.
         Let's use exact pre-calculated nice pixel coordinates that look proportional and geometric:
    -->

    <!-- We can define standard positions visually correct for the problem: -->
    <!-- B = (210, 430) -->
    <!-- D = (210, 270)  [BD = 160 px] -->
    <!-- C = (330, 330)  [CD, BC placed to satisfy angles visually and label them] -->
    <!-- Let's hand-place coordinates for a clean, non-overlapping, professional exam diagram: -->

    <!-- B: (200, 420) -->
    <!-- D: (200, 250) -->
    <!-- C: (310, 340) -->
    <!-- A: (110, 200) -->

    <!-- Let's check visual aesthetics: -->
    <!-- Line BD (vertical): (200, 420) to (200, 250) -->
    <!-- North extension from D: (200, 250) to (200, 160) -->
    <!-- Triangle BCD: B(200,420), C(315, 330), D(200,250) -->
    <!-- Triangle ABD: A(115, 190), B(200,420), D(200,250) -->

    <!-- Lines / Polygon -->
    <polygon points="115,190 200,420 315,330 200,250" fill="none" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.75" />
    <line x1="200,420" y1="420" x2="200,250" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.75" /> <!-- BD diagonal -->

    <!-- North arrow at D -->
    <line x1="200" y1="250" x2="200" y2="155" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#arrow)" />
    <text x="205" y="150" font-style="italic" font-size="16">N</text>

    <!-- Point dots -->
    <circle cx="200" cy="420" r="3.5" fill="black" />
    <circle cx="315" cy="330" r="3.5" fill="black" />
    <circle cx="200" cy="250" r="3.5" fill="black" />
    <circle cx="115" cy="190" r="3.5" fill="black" />

    <!-- Labels for points -->
    <text x="180" y="440" font-style="italic">B</text>
    <text x="325" y="340" font-style="italic">C</text>
    <text x="212" y="255" font-style="italic">D</text>
    <text x="95" y="190" font-style="italic">A</text>

    <!-- Side length labels -->
    <!-- AB = 14.5 m -->
    <text x="135" y="295" font-style="normal">14.5 m</text>
    <!-- AD = 6 m -->
    <text x="140" y="210" font-style="normal">6 m</text>
    <!-- CD = 9 m -->
    <text x="270" y="275" font-style="normal">9 m</text>

    <!-- Angle arcs and labels -->
    <!-- ∠DBC = 30° at B. Between BD (straight up) and BC. -->
    <path d="M 200 380 A 40 40 0 0 1 228 385" fill="none" stroke="black" stroke-width="1" />
    <text x="235" y="380" font-style="normal">30°</text>

    <!-- ∠DCB = 85° at C. Between CB and CD. -->
    <path d="M 285 325 A 35 35 0 0 0 280 295" fill="none" stroke="black" stroke-width="1" />
    <!-- Let's position the 85° text clearly near C -->
    <text x="248" y="318" font-style="normal">85°</text>

    <!-- Level ground indicator or subtle decorative context if needed - none required, standard O-level style -->

  </g>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 650 550" width="650" height="550">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="white" />

  <defs>
    <!-- Arrowhead for North arrow -->
    <marker id="arrow" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="10" refX="5" refY="5" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M 0 10 L 5 0 L 10 10 z" fill="black" />
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <g font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" fill="black">
    <!-- Lines / Polygon for quadrilateral ABDC / ACBD -->
    <!-- B = (200, 420) -->
    <!-- D = (200, 250) -->
    <!-- C = (315, 330) -->
    <!-- A = (115, 190) -->
    
    <!-- Outer polygon AB, BC, CD, DA -->
    <polygon points="115,190 200,420 315,330 200,250" fill="none" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.75" />
    <!-- Diagonal BD -->
    <line x1="200" y1="420" x2="200" y2="250" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.75" /> 

    <!-- Vertical pole CT at C (height 12 m, drawn vertically upwards/perpendicularly) -->
    <!-- C is at (315, 330). Let's draw pole upwards to (315, 230) -->
    <line x1="315" y1="330" x2="315" y2="230" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" />
    <text x="325" y="285" font-style="normal">12 m</text>
    <!-- Point T at top of pole -->
    <circle cx="315" cy="230" r="3" fill="black" />
    <text x="322" y="228" font-style="italic">T</text>

    <!-- North arrow at D -->
    <line x1="200" y1="250" x2="200" y2="155" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#arrow)" />
    <text x="205" y="150" font-style="italic" font-size="16">N</text>

    <!-- Point dots -->
    <circle cx="200" cy="420" r="3.5" fill="black" />
    <circle cx="315" cy="330" r="3.5" fill="black" />
    <circle cx="200" cy="250" r="3.5" fill="black" />
    <circle cx="115" cy="190" r="3.5" fill="black" />

    <!-- Labels for points -->
    <text x="180" y="440" font-style="italic">B</text>
    <text x="328" y="345" font-style="italic">C</text>
    <text x="212" y="255" font-style="italic">D</text>
    <text x="95" y="190" font-style="italic">A</text>

    <!-- Side length labels -->
    <!-- AB = 14.5 m -->
    <text x="135" y="295" font-style="normal">14.5 m</text>
    <!-- AD = 6 m -->
    <text x="140" y="210" font-style="normal">6 m</text>
    <!-- CD = 9 m -->
    <text x="270" y="275" font-style="normal">9 m</text>

    <!-- Angle arcs and labels -->
    <!-- ∠DBC = 30° at B. Between BD (straight up) and BC. -->
    <path d="M 200 380 A 40 40 0 0 1 228 385" fill="none" stroke="black" stroke-width="1" />
    <text x="235" y="380" font-style="normal">30°</text>

    <!-- ∠DCB = 85° at C. Between CB and CD. -->
    <path d="M 285 325 A 35 35 0 0 0 280 295" fill="none" stroke="black" stroke-width="1" />
    <text x="248" y="318" font-style="normal">85°</text>

  </g>
</svg>
